# Shamir Network Leakage

This repository studies information-theoretic secrecy of unchanged classical Shamir sharing against one classical leaked bit per device, assisted by independent bipartite quantum sources on arbitrary graphs. It includes an arbitrary external-reference guarantee and an exact even-device full-threshold optimum in a narrower reference model.

## Reading routes

- Scientific question and result table: README.md
- Connected scientific explanation and proof dependencies: science/README.md
- Shares, quantum resources, classical flags, reference scopes and distance convention: science/model.md
- Input Fourier expansion, dual MDS code and output-parity identities: science/fourier.md
- Inherited complex graph contraction and second-/fourth-moment coefficient bounds: science/network_bounds.md
- Full-threshold bounds, finite-prime cosine factor and matching attack: science/full_threshold.md
- General-threshold finite bounds, optimization and sufficient asymptotic rates: science/general_threshold.md
- Coherent-purification counterexample, communication and source-graph distinction: science/boundaries.md
- Primary-source comparison and precise inherited ingredients: references/RELATED_WORK.md
- Structured bibliography: references/references.bib
- Reproduction commands and interpretation: verification/README.md

## Distinctions to preserve

The public inputs and outputs are classical. Arbitrary local quantum processing does not mean quantum leaked outputs. The resource is independent of the secret and sharing randomness, and leakage occurs without communication or adversary feedback.

An adversary that is another vertex of the independent bipartite-source graph has a different resource scope from an adversary holding an arbitrary extension of the product-source device marginal. Only the narrower scope has the exact even-device bound proportional to 2^(-n/2). The arbitrary-reference theorem supplies an upper bound proportional to 2^(-n/4), whose optimality is not established.

The general-threshold numbers are sufficient rates from explicit finite bounds. They are not optimal thresholds and are not improvements over all classical leakage rates. An actual classical seed is treated branchwise; coherent purification of an unlabelled mixture is a different resource.

Quantum Finner, the complex contraction, Shamir Fourier methods, paired frequencies, the MDS inequality and minimum-distance weighting are inherited ingredients. The added scientific conclusion is the scoped secrecy guarantee for dense overlapping independent-source networks. Use the related-work page for attribution and model comparisons.

The written proofs establish uniform claims. Finite enumerations and numerical optimizations establish only the checks described in verification/README.md.
